title: Finite-free coefficient Hom is the identity in evaluation coordinates
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, nonnegative indices m≤n, and an arbitrary scheme T. Let A and B be the lifted coefficient rings at positive exponents n+1 and m+1, with canonical quotient φ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow]. Work in the ordinary small-etale unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For arbitrary objects K,N, the canonical evaluation-transpose comparison v satisfies LisseHomLocalFreeCalculationRing [def-sf-finite-free-hom-local-calculation]: for every finite-free degree-zero trivialization of K and every bounded flat representative P of N, the source and target evaluation coordinates are invertible and v followed by target coordinates equals source coordinates. This includes rank zero and identity quotients. The existential arrow is required to be heterogeneously equal to the specified canonical arrow, so asserts no choice of data.

proof.text: For a supplied trivialization K=A^t[0], its standard basis displays K as the finite coproduct of units. Tensoring on the right preserves that coproduct. The tensor-Hom adjunction therefore displays Hom(K,N) as the product of t copies of N, with precisely the evaluation coordinates of [def-sf-finite-free-hom-evaluation-coordinates].

proof.text: Bounded flat P is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The canonical derived scalar counit on P is invertible [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Scalar extension is additive and hence preserves finite products. Thus all model maps in the source coordinates are invertible. The reduced basis is again a coproduct basis because scalar extension preserves coproducts and the scalar unit is invertible.

proof.text: Compose the required identity with each product projection. By [def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow], v is the transpose of reduced evaluation. Naturality of the tensorator in the chosen basis vector and its unit constraint identify this component with scalar extension of evaluation at that vector, followed by the representative map. Product uniqueness proves the identity. The empty family gives the unique map between zero objects.

theorem etaleFiniteFreeHomLocalIdentity (T : Scheme.{u}) {n m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n)
    (K N : finiteHomEtale l E T n) :
    ∃ v : LisseHomComparisonType
      (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
      (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (m + 1)))
      (finiteHomQuotient l E h) T K N,
      HEq v (etaleFiniteHomCanonical l E T h K N) ∧
      LisseHomLocalFreeCalculationRing _ _ (finiteHomQuotient l E h) T K N v
